observation_definitions.header_observed: HTTP status line and header terminator are received; this never establishes startup success.
observation_definitions.first_valid_byte: The first byte after the HTTP header terminator that is accepted by the byte-validity predicate.
observation_definitions.first_valid_frame: The earliest body prefix accepted by an explicit frame-validity predicate; the conservative default accepts no body as a frame.
observation_definitions.startup_success: true only when first_valid_frame is observed before first_frame_deadline and without timeout, cancellation, or read error.
observation_definitions.resource_sample: A timestamped process/resource snapshot with raw values; deltas are computed only between samples from the same run.
observation_definitions.clock: Monotonic elapsed seconds are authoritative for deadlines; wall-clock timestamps are reporting-only.
observation_definitions.timeout: A deadline is exceeded when monotonic elapsed time is greater than or equal to the configured boundary.
observation_definitions.cancellation: Cancellation is terminal, records the cancellation timestamp/reason, and cannot be converted to startup success.
observation_definitions.errors: Operational failures are preserved as structured error strings and yield ERROR unless cancellation or timeout is the recorded terminal state.

fixture.reason: HTTP headers without a valid byte/frame must not win startup.

red_green.red: Against the permissive default, headers plus non-frame junk incorrectly reports PASS and first_valid_frame; the regression requires FAIL with first_valid_frame unset.
red_green.green: P07-01 keeps first_valid_byte distinct from first_valid_frame, requires an explicit frame validator, records declared-end boundaries, and preserves cancellation, errors, and resource samples.
